svg.text: REFERENCE ONLY — resistance-to-accident figures, not a fabrication drawing
HOW HARD YOU HAVE TO HIT IT
Force to shift or unseat the mount, by direction and magnet count. Each cell is lb on top, newtons below.
Every magnet is a 32 mm pot magnet derated to 26.2 lb on painted appliance sheet (75 lb rated).
These are resistance-to-ACCIDENT numbers, not removal forces — peeling one corner beats them all at 26 lb.
The magnets carry NO vertical load. The hook does. This table is about shifting the plate, not holding the screen up.
grab the BOTTOM edge and pull
grab the TOP edge and pull
lift the whole thing straight UP
press the screen edge to twist it off
it MOVES the mount rather than detaching it — the hook does not resist that axis, and mu is only 0.2 on bare nickel.
Doubling the magnets does NOT double the resistance

peel and twist depend on WHERE a magnet sits, not just how many there are. The four corners are already the best positions on the plate; mid-sides sit on a centreline and contribute nothing to rotation about it.
A firm touch press is about 5 lb (22 N)
compare that against the twist row — that is the governing everyday load.
